name: Facet
text: I’ll spin up a local dev server to audit the current interface’s visibility and accessibility baseline. First, I’ll clone the repo (`git clone https://github.com/org/repo.git`), then run `npm install` and `npm run dev` to spin up the interface on `localhost:3000`. I’ll use Lighthouse CI (`npm install -g @lhci/cli && lhci autorun`) to generate a full audit report, targeting a minimum 90% score for accessibility and performance. If the report flags any critical issues, I’ll log them in `audit-issues.md` and flag them for the team lead to review.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Hold—before we default to a local dev server, what’s the *real* baseline you’re auditing against? The repo’s `main` branch could already be stale, or worse, the accessibility issues might be in the *design system* upstream that this repo consumes. Where’s the evidence that the repo’s current state reflects the *live* interface’s visibility/accessibility? Demand a screenshot of the Lighthouse report *before* any local spin-up—otherwise, we’re optimizing blind.
